author: human
request:
Feature request: filter the vet list by specialty. Three product decisions
come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-9 is narrowed: free-text veterinarian search stays out of
  scope, but filtering the directory by an attribute it already shows is in.
  Record the narrowing the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The JSON endpoint at /vets is reinstated as a supported surface — this
  filter is its first requested capability. Mint a fresh requirement for it;
  the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused.
- The filter is a URL contract only. Neither surface gains a form, dropdown,
  or other page control in this request; pagination links carry the
  parameter so filtered pages stay navigable. A visible control may come as
  a follow-up request.

Both vet list surfaces accept an optional `specialty` query parameter:

- /vets.html?specialty=<name> — the HTML page shows only vets holding that
  specialty; pagination applies to the filtered list.
- /vets?specialty=<name> — the JSON endpoint returns only those vets.

Matching is on the whole specialty name, case-insensitive — not a prefix. A
specialty matching no vet yields the normal page or JSON document with an
empty vet list (HTTP 200). An empty or whitespace-only value behaves as if
the parameter were absent, like the empty owner search. Without the parameter
both endpoints behave as today. Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Veterinarian directory: narrow both vet list surfaces to one specialty
summary: A reader narrows the HTML veterinarian directory and the reinstated machine-readable veterinarian list to the veterinarians holding one named specialty, requested through the address alone. Matching is on the whole specialty name, ignoring letter case; without a usable name both surfaces behave as today.
acceptance_criteria: [REQ-VET-003] /vets.html?specialty=<name> lists only veterinarians holding that specialty; pagination applies to the narrowed list (page count and total reflect it).
[REQ-VET-003] /vets?specialty=<name> returns only veterinarians holding that specialty in the machine-readable form.
[REQ-VET-003] Matching is on the whole specialty name, case-insensitive, on both surfaces: 'RADIOLOGY' and 'Radiology' match radiology; a prefix such as 'radio' matches no veterinarian.
[REQ-VET-003] A specialty name no veterinarian holds yields the usual page or machine-readable document with an empty veterinarian list and HTTP 200, on both surfaces.
[REQ-VET-003] An empty or whitespace-only specialty value behaves exactly as if the parameter were absent, on both surfaces.
[REQ-VET-003] Every pagination link on a narrowed directory page carries the same specialty parameter, so following it keeps the narrowing.
[REQ-VET-003] Edge case 2: a narrowed veterinarian holding other specialties too is shown with all of them, not only the requested one.
[REQ-VET-003] Edge case 3: a veterinarian holding no specialty never appears in a narrowed result on either surface.
[REQ-VET-003] Edge case 4: narrowing by the word the directory shows for a veterinarian with no specialty ('none') lists no veterinarian.
[REQ-VET-004] Without the parameter, the machine-readable form returns every veterinarian with their specialties, as today; the HTML directory without the parameter is unchanged (REQ-VET-001).
non_goals: Any form, dropdown, or other page control for choosing a specialty on either surface; the owner decided the filter is a URL contract only, and a visible control may come as a follow-up request.
Free-text veterinarian search, and searching for a pet or a visit (NG-9 as narrowed).
Narrowing by more than one specialty in one request (open question in docs/prd.md).
Any matching rule for a specialty name with leading or trailing spaces beyond the blank-value rule (open question in docs/prd.md).
Any on-page indication of which specialty a narrowed directory shows (open question in docs/prd.md).
Paging the machine-readable form, or any other change to either surface when the parameter is absent.
notes: Requirement allocation: REQ-VET-003 is the specialty narrowing across both surfaces; REQ-VET-004 is the fresh requirement the owner asked to mint for the reinstated machine-readable veterinarian list (already implemented; this slice only proves its unfiltered baseline). REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn in the Superseded list, with a pointer to REQ-VET-004. REQ-VET-001 edge case 2 (the 'route serves no requirement' known defect) is replaced; no test cited it. For system-design-expert: docs/system-design.md still describes the machine-readable route as serving no requirement (overview, contracts table REQ column, known-defects row) and needs updating to REQ-VET-004/REQ-VET-003. docs/adr/README.md needs an index row for docs/adr/2026-09-11-non-goal-narrow-veterinarian-search.md; that file is outside this agent's write scope. Test names: the existing showResourcesVetList may be strengthened and renamed to theVetResourceListShouldReturnEveryVetWithTheirSpecialties per docs/testing-principles.md; the matching-rule, empty-result, and blank-value tests may each be data-driven across both surfaces. The owner stated no further product answer will come; open questions (visible control, several specialties, surrounding spaces, active-filter indication) are recorded in docs/prd.md Open Questions, and the narrowest reading was taken for each.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Stays inside the vet feature package (system-design § Package Structure); no new type, module, or dependency. The narrowing extends the paged derived-query pattern owner search already uses (OwnerRepository.findByLastNameStartingWith) to VetRepository, in a paged form for /vets.html and an unpaged form for /vets. New ground recorded in ADR 2026-09-11-veterinarian-narrowing-as-uncached-repository-query: letter case folds inside the query (vendor-independent, unlike the PostgreSQL owner-search defect), each veterinarian is returned once, the narrowed reads carry no cache, and VetController holds no matching logic, only blank-as-absent binding. system-design.md now records the reinstated machine-readable route under REQ-VET-004 (overview, Contracts rows for Vet/Specialty/Vets/VetRepository/VetController/CacheConfiguration, Security Context inputs and outputs). The route's known-defect row is removed, the narrowing paragraph sits under Contracts invariants, the case-folding paragraph under Persistence, and two Threat Model rows are added. docs/adr/README.md indexes both 2026-09-11 ADRs (the product expert's NG-9 non-goal ADR and this one). Claims rest on direct reads of VetController, VetRepository, Vet, Vets, CacheConfiguration, vetList.html, VetControllerTests and the H2 seed data. The IDE oracle was not connected, so no symbol-resolution call backs them.
integration_points: Repository boundary (VetRepository): gains a paged and an unpaged derived query narrowing to the holders of one specialty by whole name with letter case folded in the query, distinct (e.g. findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String, Pageable) and (String)); keep @Transactional(readOnly = true), omit @Cacheable (ADR 2026-09-11-veterinarian-narrowing-as-uncached-repository-query). Double: the real VetRepository over the seeded embedded H2, in a full application context (@SpringBootTest + @AutoConfigureMockMvc). VetControllerTests converts from @WebMvcTest + @MockitoBean VetRepository and retires the stub, because a stub cannot prove a rule that lives in a query (ADR Consequences; testing-principles § Mocking Policy). Seed coverage: radiology = Helen Leary, Henry Stevens; surgery = Linda Douglas, Rafael Ortega; dentistry = Linda Douglas; no specialty = James Carter, Sharon Jenkins; six veterinarians, page size 5, so the unnarrowed directory spans two pages.

Page-link test (theVetDirectoryPageLinksShouldKeepTheSpecialtyFilter): no seeded specialty has more than two holders, so no seeded narrowed list spans two pages. The test owns its rows: in a rolled-back test transaction it inserts, through JdbcTemplate, a test-only specialty held by at least six veterinarians. It then issues only narrowed requests. Still a real repository over real H2, no stub.

Transport boundary: MockMvc drives both routes, the one sanctioned mock (CLAUDE.md Testing Strategy; testing-principles § Mocking Policy). The JSON assertions go through jsonPath on the existing Vets root (vetList), whose shape stays unchanged for REQ-VET-004.

Binding, GET /vets.html and GET /vets (existing entry points, no new route): each binds an optional specialty as @RequestParam(required = false) String, a request-scoped scalar. No persisted type is bound from it: no Specialty model attribute, formatter, or lookup. A blank value (null, empty, or whitespace-only; StringUtils.hasText) selects the unnarrowed read; any other value passes to the repository unchanged. The page parameter binding stays as it is.

Template (vets/vetList.html): each of the page, first, previous, next, and last links carries the active specialty as a Thymeleaf link-expression parameter, e.g. @{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})}. The controller adds the normalized specialty (absent when blank) to the model for this use only. Nothing on the page displays it (PRD Open Questions: no active-filter indication). The model attributes currentPage, totalPages, totalItems, and listVets come from the narrowed Page.

patterns.description: Paged derived query taking the search text and a Pageable. It is the precedent for the narrowed paged read, and consistency over novelty (architecture-principles § Design Principles 2) rules out a second paging mechanism.
findPaginated / addPaginationModel: the page size and the four model attributes. The narrowed directory reuses both; pass the chosen Page in rather than duplicating the helpers.

processFindForm normalizes optional search text at the boundary before the query. It is the precedent for blank-as-absent. Unlike owner search, a non-blank specialty is not stripped (ADR Consequences; see notes).

risks.risk: Adding @Cacheable("vets") to the narrowed reads, for consistency with the other VetRepository methods, keys the unbounded Caffeine/JCache cache on caller text: any caller grows memory without limit.
risks.mitigation: Leave both narrowed queries uncached (ADR 2026-09-11-veterinarian-narrowing-as-uncached-repository-query; system-design § Threat Model, memory-exhaustion row; security-principles § Trust Boundaries, external-input row, and Realization, widening-the-exposed-surface row).

risks.risk: The join through specialties can repeat a veterinarian: specialty names carry no uniqueness constraint and vet_specialties has no primary key. A repeated veterinarian would inflate totalItems/totalPages and break the page-count criterion.
risks.mitigation: Distinct derived query, whose generated count is distinct as well (system-design § Persistence, narrowing paragraph).

risks.risk: Edge case 2: a fetch join filtered by the requested name would load only the matched specialty, so the veterinarian would render truncated.
risks.mitigation: Filter through a plain join only and leave the existing EAGER specialties mapping to load the full set (system-design § Persistence, eager associations under open-in-view off). Prove it against the real repository: narrowing by dentistry shows Linda Douglas with dentistry and surgery.

risks.risk: The reflected specialty reaches page links. String-concatenating it into the href (the current links use the '/vets.html?page=__${i}__' literal form) would skip URL encoding and let a crafted value inject parameters or markup.
risks.mitigation: Use link-expression parameters only; never concatenate the value into a URL string or render it as text (security-principles § Realization, cross-site scripting row; system-design § Threat Model, reflected-specialty row).

risks.risk: The unnarrowed directory must stay unchanged (REQ-VET-004 criterion; REQ-VET-001). A null link parameter can render as a bare 'specialty' name in the href, which would alter today's links.
risks.mitigation: Emit the specialty parameter only while a narrowing is active; unnarrowed links render exactly as today. Assert the unnarrowed hrefs carry no specialty.

risks.risk: Letter-case matching that rests on column collation diverges per vendor, as PostgreSQL owner search already does (system-design § Known Defects).
risks.mitigation: Fold case in the query (IgnoreCase in the derived query), never through column typing (system-design § Persistence, narrowing paragraph).

risks.risk: The page-link test's inserted rows could leak into the shared context's vet cache if that test issues an unnarrowed request, poisoning later tests after rollback.
risks.mitigation: That test issues narrowed requests only; narrowed reads are uncached by design (ADR Decision).

risks.risk: Placing the matching in the controller, as an in-memory filter over findAll(), adds a business rule to a web controller and hand-rolled paging.
risks.mitigation: Controller branches only on blank versus non-blank and delegates (architecture-principles § Pattern Catalog, Web controller row; system-design § Contracts, narrowing paragraph).

risks.risk: A hand-written JPQL string built from the request value would open injection.
risks.mitigation: Derived queries only, bound parameters (security-principles § Realization, injection row; system-design § Threat Model, SQL injection row).

notes: Owner-open choices, narrowest reading taken (the owner stated no further product answer will come). (1) A non-blank specialty with surrounding spaces is passed unchanged and so matches nothing. PRD Open Questions leaves the case open, and no test pins it; recorded in the ADR Consequences. (2) Narrowed reads keep the unnarrowed reads' ordering: none is imposed, the same as today's findAll(Pageable). Tests must not assert order beyond what they control. (3) The existing showResourcesVetList may be strengthened and renamed to theVetResourceListShouldReturnEveryVetWithTheirSpecialties, asserting all six seeded veterinarians and Linda Douglas's two specialties. The matching, empty-result, and blank-value tests may each run data-driven across both surfaces (prd-entry notes). Product-expert items resolved in design scope: system-design.md no longer calls the machine-readable route requirement-less (overview, Contracts Implements column, Known Defects row removed, provenance banner now counts three confirmed defects), and docs/adr/README.md indexes docs/adr/2026-09-11-non-goal-narrow-veterinarian-search.md. The SSR ADR 2026-07-31-server-side-rendering-with-thymeleaf already records this route as the one departure from rendered pages, so reinstating it contradicts no recorded decision. Open Question 5 (vet cache invalidation) is unaffected: the narrowed reads never enter the cache. No design-doc-autofix records exist to audit.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Injection into data access: the request-supplied specialty reaches the database only as a bound argument to Spring Data derived queries (VetRepository.java diff: `Collection<Vet> findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String specialtyName)` and the paged overload). No query text is concatenated. The IgnoreCase derivation is an equality match, not LIKE, so `%` and `_` are not wildcards; VetControllerTests `radiologySpellingsOnEachSurface` asserts that the prefix `radio` yields no vets on both surfaces.

Reflected-parameter XSS and parameter injection: the specialty reaches vetList.html only as a link-expression parameter, e.g. `@{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})}` inside th:href. Thymeleaf URL-encodes the parameter and escapes the attribute, and the full-template read shows no th:text or th:utext that prints it. `theVetDirectoryPageLinksShouldKeepTheSpecialtyFilter` round-trips `ear, nose & throat` through the links and gets back exactly one decoded specialty parameter.

The diff removes Thymeleaf preprocessing from every page link. The old `@{'/vets.html?page=__${i}__'}` forms become parameterized link expressions, and `grep -F '__$'` over the current vetList.html returns no hits. This does not replace a control; it strengthens the template.

Memory exhaustion through caller-chosen cache keys: both narrowed repository methods carry `@Transactional(readOnly = true)` and no `@Cacheable`. Only the existing fixed-key `@Cacheable("vets")` reads stay cached, which matches the system-design Threat Model row for REQ-VET-003 and its ADR. The unpaginated narrowed JSON read is bounded by the same data set as the existing `findAll()`.

No new request binding: the change adds only simple `@RequestParam(required = false) String specialty` parameters, with no `@ModelAttribute` or `@RequestBody` target, so the binding and mass-assignment checklist does not apply. No logging, file I/O, process execution, or Jackson type configuration is added (VetController.java and VetRepository.java diff hunks read in full).

Credentials: `git diff HEAD -- src/ docs/ | grep -i -E '^\+.*(password|secret|token|apikey|api_key|credential|private.?key)'` hits only the docs/system-design.md Security Context prose line about environment-supplied datasource credentials. No secret is added.

Supply chain: build.gradle is not in the change set (`scripts/changeset.sh --name-only`), so no dependency changes. dependencyCheckAnalyze is not configured (`grep -F dependencyCheck build.gradle` returns nothing), so no NVD match ran in this review. `./gradlew dependencies` resolves Spring Boot 4.1.1, spring-webmvc 7.0.9, Thymeleaf 3.1.5.RELEASE, jackson-databind 3.1.5, hibernate-core 7.4.5.Final, and tomcat-embed-core 11.0.24.

Pattern consistency: the blank-as-absent rule (`StringUtils.hasText`) matches the owner search's handling of an empty query, as the controller Javadoc states. The test-only JdbcTemplate inserts use `?` placeholders.

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: The model attribute holding the active narrowing (`specialty`, added at VetController.java:51 and read on every page link) reuses the exact name already bound by the per-vet loop `th:each="specialty : ${vet.specialties}"` at line 20, which iterates `Specialty` entities in the vet table above. Thymeleaf scopes the loop variable to that `<span>` so the two never actually collide at runtime, but the same identifier now means two unrelated things in one template file — a single `Specialty` entity in one block, the free-text narrowing string in another. A future reader skimming `${specialty}` in the pagination block has to trace back through the whole file to learn it is not the per-vet iteration variable.

author: change-grader
summary: narrow both veterinarian lists by specialty

blast_radius.note: The code change stays inside the vet package (VetController, VetRepository, vetList.html, one test class) and only adds an optional request parameter. The unnarrowed paths still make the same cached findAll calls, and the unnarrowed page links still render /vets.html?page=N, which a test pins. Most of the 55 hunks come from the test rewrite and the docs.

semantic_surprise.note: Reading the hunks turned up no hidden behavior change. Narrowing is an equality, case-folded, DISTINCT derived query that is deliberately uncached, blank counts as absent through hasText, and the reflected name reaches the page only as a URL-encoded link parameter. Two edges are not surprises but are worth knowing: surrounding spaces are passed through untrimmed (recorded as an open question), and the narrowed paged query has no ORDER BY, the same as the existing findAll(Pageable).

test_adequacy.note: The tests moved from a mocked repository to @SpringBootTest over the seeded H2 data. They assert real outcomes on both surfaces: case-insensitive whole-name match, prefix non-match, empty result, blank as absent, all specialties kept, specialty-less vets excluded, and page links carrying a reserved-character name across two real pages. One small gap: nothing pins the 'each vet listed once' DISTINCT guarantee, and the class drops @DisabledInNativeImage/@DisabledInAotMode without a native run to confirm.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four reviewers approved and left no recommendations. Security's absence from round 2 is expected under the fix-delta plan. However, the doc-reviewer's round-1 approval cites locations that do not resolve: docs/adr/README.md:98-99 in a 74-line file (the entries are at 73-74), and Contracts rows at system-design.md:209-214 (they are at 102-107). Reading the docs diff myself, the underlying claims hold.

scope_deviation.note: The diff matches the three recorded intake decisions: NG-9 is narrowed through a non-goal ADR, the /vets route is reinstated under a fresh REQ-VET-004 while REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn, and there is no page control while pagination carries the parameter. There were no design revisions and no consultations. The single build retry was a partial checkpoint before the gate, not a failed build.

rationale: The code is contained and additive, and its tests exercise real persistence. The one flag is the doc-reviewer's approval, whose line citations do not resolve. The human should read the docs diff directly (NG-9 rewording, the REQ-VET-004 reinstatement, the removed Known Defects row) rather than lean on that approval, then glance over the code.
